description: The Green Roof Innovation Testing Laboratory, GRIT Lab, is a rooftop research facility at the University of Toronto's John H. Daniels Faculty of Architecture, Landscape, and Design that tests how green roofs, green walls and photovoltaic arrays perform in a cold climate. After Toronto's 2009 Green Roof Bylaw, it set up 33 test modules on a 4,000 square foot roof to compare growing media type and depth, planting and irrigation regimes against stormwater retention, evaporative cooling, biodiversity and life cycle cost. Each module has eight sensors, 264 in all, alongside an on-site weather station. Coverage is one roof in Toronto, built from 2010 to 2012. It won an ASLA Award of Excellence in research in 2013. Format and access: the lab site lists publications, posters and a performance index; the award statement says a data sharing portal and live feed were planned. Licence: not stated; free to read. Caveats: some lab pages no longer load, and raw data were not found. It informs climate adaptation standards for green roofs. Related catalogue records are the Hamburg Green Roof Strategy and the Basel green roofs case.

name: GRIT Lab, Green Roof Innovation Testing Laboratory (University of Toronto)
outcomes: Early results showed supplemental irrigation is needed to keep plant diversity and that grass and forb cover and biomass were greater in organic growing media, to inform Toronto's Green Roof Construction Standard.
